name: olai-plugin-odu
//name: UNSCOPED, for `olai-plugin-kolu`'s reason one appliance over: `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai, and a tenant is named the way a plugin written outside this tree would be. The directory carries the same word.
//exports: SIX entries, and three of them are DISJOINT graphs — it is `olai-plugin-kolu`'s manifest one appliance over, deliberately the same shape. `./wire` is the declaration everything that composes or reads the surface pulls in statically. `./browser` is what REPLACED the manifest: a Cordis plugin (`name`, `inject`, `apply`) registering this package's faces — the chip, the run matrix, the words beside them, and the tab's one subscription — into the app's declared slots, where the root used to be an `OlaiPlugin` object a compiled-in registry held. It carries SolidJS and it is a CHUNK, fetched only when the roster says this plugin is running, so a serve without odu never evaluates a line of it. The ROOT is the wire identity and nothing more, now that there is no manifest for it to be. `./server` is the runtime half, its own door for that exact reason: a process that renders nothing must not pull a UI runtime, which is the claim `packages/bundle/src/fence.test.ts` walks rather than trusts. The last two are the browser half's two contracts with packages that never import it: `./testids` is NAMES ONLY, so a scenario asserts on this package's own DOM without pulling a component into a suite that has no browser, and `./all.css` is the sheet — a `@source` pointed at the faces' own directory, because Tailwind emits only what it can SEE and a moved component nothing points at renders with no layout and nothing errors.
//: THE ODU TENANT — the CI probe, the run cell, the chip and matrix that draw it, and the run events that reach the feed. It wraps `@olai/odu-client`, which stays the only package that names `@odu/*`.
//dependencies: `@olai/odu-client`, `@olai/format`, `solid-js` and `@olai/plugin-api` — the last of which arrived when the registry left that package for `@olai/bundle`, exactly as `olai-plugin-kolu`.s manifest records one appliance over. `./server` names the services it injects and gets `ctx.vault` typed by declaration merging; nothing here imports a registry, which is what keeps the arrow one-way. `@olai/format` is here because `worktrees.ts` is — the walk that asks which nodes name a worktree, and whether the vault DECLARED that key a path, reads outline records: a thing `@olai/odu-client` must not learn (its interfaces are parametric in the node type) and a judgement `@olai/server` has no business making, since what it licences is a socket dial in somebody's checkout. `solid-js` is a runtime dependency here rather than a type-only one, because this package OWNS its browser faces — odu has no `-ui` sibling, and it needs none: nothing it draws reaches odu's product tier, so there is no second wall for a second package to be. What is deliberately NOT here is `@olai/web`: the faces need the app's clock, its duration register and the drawer's own contract, and every one of those arrives as a VALUE (src/browser/app.ts declares the shapes structurally and argues why) rather than as an import that would be a cycle.
//devDependencies: @olai/surface for its `./testlib` door ONLY — the schema walk that holds this cell`s `arrayKey` declaration honest (src/wire.test.ts). Deliberately not a runtime dependency, and it could not be one: surface sits ABOVE the plugin packages now, so a real dependency here would be the cycle the composition is shaped to make unrepresentable. A testlib is the one thing that can travel the other way, because nothing it touches ships.
